name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005841220

head_commit.message:
Nsight Systems (`nsys` 2026.3+ and 2026.5.2) projects build-time NVTX ranges onto top-level `FUSION` and `COLLECTIVES_KERNEL` CUDA Graph nodes in `--cuda-graph-trace=node` mode, but drops NVTX attribution for child-graph command types (`CUBLAS`, `CUBLASLT`, `CUDNN`, `CUSTOM_CALL`, `DYNAMIC_SLICE_FUSION`) and `CONDITIONAL` graphs.

Detect Nsight Systems (`NSYS_PROFILING_SESSION_ID` or `NSYS_NVTX_PROFILER_REGISTER_ONLY`) in `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` in xla/debug_options_flags.cc and default `xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` to `{COLLECTIVES_KERNEL, FUSION}`, honoring explicit `--xla_gpu_enable_command_buffer` overrides. On an H100 `t5x` step, HLO op attribution rises from 97.47% (731/750) of kernels and 76.87% of GPU kernel time to 100% (750/750) at +0.25% (+12.83 us) step time.

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

head_commit.message:
Register fallback NVTX instruction titles and support compact XLA domain ranges.

`GetInstructionAnnotation` previously passed an unregistered `std::string` to `ScopedAnnotation` outside `ScopedModuleAnnotations`, preventing Nsight Systems `--capture-range=nvtx` from matching fallback thunk ranges. Also, `pgo_nsys_converter.py` used a greedy `hlo_op=(.*)#` regex that captured trailing `,unique_hlo_op_id=...` metadata.

Add `tsl::profiler::RangePush(ProfilerDomainHandle, StringHandle)` and cache registered fallback handles in `GetInstructionAnnotation`. Add `tsl::profiler::XlaProfilerDomain()` and `NvtxRangeFormat::kHloOpName` (selected when `XLA_GPU_NVTX_DOMAIN=XLA`) to emit compact `<hlo_op>` NVTX titles in the `XLA` domain while keeping `xprof_name()` in `Thunk:#...#` format. Update `pgo_nsys_converter.py` to stop at `,` or `#` and accept `XLA:<hlo_op>` ranges.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Set unique collective op_id on CPU and compute per-call Gloo tags.

head_commit.message:
Set unique collective op_id on CPU and compute per-call Gloo tags.

Previously, `ThunkEmitter` set `op_id` on every collective thunk to `channel_id` when present or to the module ID otherwise, and `GlooCommunicator` hardcoded `tag = 0` on all collective operations. While the presence of `channel_id` (`has_channel_id`) still selects the collective group mode (such as `CROSS_PARTITION` or `FLATTENED_ID`), its numeric value was originally meant for matching collectives across separate modules in MPMD programs. In modern single-module SPMD programs, passes often set a constant dummy `channel_id` (such as `1`) just to mark `has_channel_id = true`, which gave multiple collectives in the same module the same `op_id`.

Update `GetCollectiveOpParams` in `xla/service/cpu/thunk_emitter.cc` to set `op_id` to `instruction->unique_id()`, giving each collective instruction in a module a distinct static ID while preserving `has_channel_id` for group-mode selection. In `xla/backends/cpu/collectives/gloo_communicator.cc`, track a per-`op_id` loop counter for the active `RunId` and fingerprint `(op_id, run_id, loop_counter)` into Gloo's 32-bit tag for `AllReduce`, `CollectivePermute`, `AllToAll`, `AllGather`, and `ReduceScatter`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000509791

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, and rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated).
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

display_title: [XLA] Check element types for kReduce and kReduceWindow in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kReduce and kReduceWindow in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Check that the output subshape and corresponding `to_apply` parameter types of `kReduce` and `kReduceWindow`, as well as any `kConvert` instructions in their `to_apply` subcomputation, have a precision-preserving element type transition relative to the reduced operand (`in_type == out_type` or between `high_precision_type_` and `low_precision_type_`).

Combined with the `kConvert` check in `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision`, this prevents `BFloat16Propagation` from propagating `BF16` through `kReduce` or `kReduceWindow` when the `to_apply` subcomputation narrows or truncates values (either via `kConvert`, such as `F32 -> S32 -> F32` or `F32 -> F16 -> F32`, or implicitly via mixed-precision parameter/output types), while still allowing same-type converts, conversions between `high_precision_type_` and `low_precision_type_`, and non-`kConvert` instructions of other element types (such as `PRED` predicates or `S32` variadic branches).

display_title: Add GPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

head_commit.message:
Add GPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` were lowered as large graphs of primitive operations on GPU, which made both compilation and execution slow.

This change replaces the CUDA and ROCm implementations of `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` with GPU kernels in the GPU `_math` extension, sharing the polynomial coefficients and tables with the CPU kernels. The kernels keep the same accuracy bounds (`<= 1.0` ULP for `float16`/`float32`/`float64` and `<= 0.5` ULP for `bfloat16`) and support sharded execution, CUDA graphs, and `jax.export`.

For `float32` and 16-bit inputs, the kernel checks the device's `float32`-to-`float64` throughput ratio and promotes to `float64` on GPUs with fast double-precision hardware, falling back to a native `float32` implementation otherwise.

display_title: Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

head_commit.message:
Skip per-command NVTX annotations during in-place command buffer updates.

In-place CUDA graph node parameter updates in `CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` do not create CUDA graph nodes and are ignored by Nsight Systems CUDA graph node attribution, which associates kernel nodes with the NVTX ranges active during `RecordCreate` or cache-miss child-graph capture. Pushing a `ScopedAnnotation` around every command in `CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` emits redundant host-side NVTX ranges every step.

Remove the outer `ScopedAnnotation` from `CommandExecutor::RecordUpdate` and push it inside the `GetOrTraceCommandBuffer` trace callback in `TracedCommand::RecordTracedCommand` on `RecordUpdate`, preserving cache-miss attribution while eliminating steady-state overhead.

display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, and rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated).
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

head_commit.message:
PR #46400: [XLA:GPU] Use IEEE-754 compliant f32 division in NVPTX backend

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46400

#ai-generated

**Fixes:** #37181

**Summary of Changes**
Changed `-nvptx-prec-divf32` from `1` (`div.full`, 2 ULP error) to `2` (`div.rnd`, IEEE-754 compliant) in the NVPTX backend. LLVM already defaults to `2`; XLA was overriding it.

**Justification**
GPU float32 division produces non-IEEE-754 results: `a/a` evaluates to `0.99999994` instead of `1.0` for many f32 values. This violates user expectations and breaks numerical invariants. The issue was confirmed on RTX 3090 (JAX 0.6.0) in #37181.

**Kind of Contribution**
Bug Fix

**Benchmark**
N/A — this is a correctness fix, not a performance change. The original `=1` override was added for "float-division heavy benchmarks" but `div.full` trades correctness for speed; `div.rnd` is LLVM's default and is IEEE-754 compliant with >1 ULP accuracy.

**Unit Tests**
New regression test: `xla/tests/ieee_f32_division_test.cc` (registered as `//xla/tests:ieee_f32_division_test`, runs on cpu+gpu) asserts the IEEE-754 identity properties `x / x == 1.0` and `x / 1.0 == x` that the `div.full` override broke, across values including `FLT_MAX`, `FLT_MIN`, `1e10`, `1e-10`. It uses parameters and disabled fast math so the division is actually executed by the backend rather than folded or simplified away. Existing GPU backend tests continue to pass: `nvptx_backend_test`, `load_ir_module_test`, `utils_test`, `nvptx_utils_test`.

**Execution Tests**
A standalone reproducer script is available at `repro_xla_37181.py` that verifies IEEE-754 division compliance across 5 categories (identity, inverse, overflow, underflow, NaN).

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Add parameter buffer slices to ComputationKernelArguments.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Add parameter buffer slices to ComputationKernelArguments.

`Visit` in `ComputationKernelArguments` previously added slices to `walk.arguments` only by iterating over `instruction->operands()` and skipped `kParameter` instructions when adding `instruction` slices to `walk.results`. When a called computation has an unused `kParameter` (or a `kParameter` that is the computation root with no other users), its slice was omitted from `buffer_table_index_`, causing `IrEmitter::EmitGlobalBufferPointer` to `CHECK`-fail when `IrEmitter::HandleParameter` visited the parameter.

Explicitly add `kParameter` slices to `walk.arguments` in `Visit` so every parameter visited by `IrEmitter` has a buffer table index. Every non-thread-local slice of a walked instruction is now in the buffer table, so `Fingerprint` checks this instead of handling buffers outside the table.

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

When an operand of `tt.expand_dims` already contains a unit dimension adjacent
to the expanded axis, `triton_xla.squeeze_dims` on the pre-existing unit axis
produces the same tensor type as the `tt.expand_dims` operand. Checking type
equality instead of axis equality cancels the two ops instead of swapping them,
which stops `squeeze_dims` from reaching upstream `xtile.extract` tiles and
drops the `tt.expand_dims` before `tt.broadcast`.

Only fold `squeeze_dims(expand_dims(x))` to `x` when the axes match or `x` is a
1D unit tensor that cannot be squeezed further; otherwise swap the two ops so
unit dimensions continue propagating upward.

Previously, `CuptiErrorManager` disabled CUPTI process-wide on this error, `CuptiTracer::EnableApiTracing` set `api_tracing_enabled_` before `PrepareSubscriberForSession` succeeded, and `CuptiTracer::Disable` unconditionally dereferenced uninitialized state.

head_commit.message:
When an external tool such as Nsight Systems or Nsight Compute holds the CUPTI subscriber slot, `cuptiSubscribe` returns `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` (or `CUPTI_ERROR_MAX_LIMIT_REACHED`). Previously:

- `CuptiErrorManager::Subscribe` and `CuptiErrorManager::SubscribeV2` treated this error as fatal and called `UndoAndDisable()`, latching `disabled_ = 1` for the lifetime of the process so subsequent profiling sessions could not recover even after the external subscriber detached.
- `CuptiTracer::EnableApiTracing` called `PrepareCallbackStart()` (which set `api_tracing_enabled_ = true`) before `PrepareSubscriberForSession`, leaving `api_tracing_enabled_` set on subscription failure.
- `CuptiTracer::Disable` unconditionally called `Finalize()` and dereferenced `cupti_driver_api_hook_` and `collector_` even when `Enable()` had backed off without enabling tracing.

Update `CuptiErrorManager` and `CuptiTracer` to handle external CUPTI subscriber conflicts per session:

- Allow `CUPTI_ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGES`, `CUPTI_ERROR_MAX_LIMIT_REACHED`, and `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED` in `CuptiErrorManager::Subscribe` and `CuptiErrorManager::SubscribeV2` without disabling CUPTI process-wide.
- Move `PrepareCallbackStart()` after `PrepareSubscriberForSession()` in `CuptiTracer::EnableApiTracing()`, clear subscriber state on `Subscribe` failure, log a warning when an external subscriber is active, and return `absl::UnavailableError`.
- Reset `collector_`, `option_`, and `cupti_driver_api_hook_` in `CuptiTracer::Enable()` cleanup on failure, and guard `CuptiTracer::Disable()` when no tracing mode is enabled.

display_title: [ROCm] [CUDA] SKIP_PROFILED: allocate temp buffers in the VA reservation from the first execution PR 2/2

head_commit.message:
[ROCm] SKIP_PROFILED: allocate temp buffers in the VA reservation from the first execution

- In SKIP_PROFILED, automatically selected preallocated temp buffers are
  allocated at their VA reservation offsets from the first execution, as
  in SKIP_TEMP. A reservation created while profiling lays out every
  profile candidate (VA only); one created after the transition covers
  only the selected set.
- Before, the profiling executions took the temp from the regular VMM pool
  and the transition allocated a second copy in the reservation. The first
  copy stayed behind as stale allocator state, so each temp was held twice.
  On ROCm every peer imports each VMM mapping into its GTT, so the second
  copy overflowed GTT and multi-GPU runs hung; on CUDA it held extra device
  memory.
- Update the SKIP_PROFILED documentation in xla.proto and the class.
- Add unit tests for a reclaim-exempt temp under a one-temp PA budget, a
  shared profiling-phase reservation and a failed profiling execution;
  extend an existing test to the first execution.

- ExecutionScope stores the device ordinal it is created for; its methods
  no longer take one.
- Add unit tests for a failed allocation, an execution without teardown,
  and a teardown before an early return.

display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, and rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated).
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005776439

display_title: PR #46400: [XLA:GPU] Use IEEE-754 compliant f32 division in NVPTX backend

head_commit.message:
PR #46400: [XLA:GPU] Use IEEE-754 compliant f32 division in NVPTX backend

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/46400

#ai-generated

**Fixes:** #37181

**Summary of Changes**
Changed `-nvptx-prec-divf32` from `1` (`div.full`, 2 ULP error) to `2` (`div.rnd`, IEEE-754 compliant) in the NVPTX backend. LLVM already defaults to `2`; XLA was overriding it.

**Justification**
GPU float32 division produces non-IEEE-754 results: `a/a` evaluates to `0.99999994` instead of `1.0` for many f32 values. This violates user expectations and breaks numerical invariants. The issue was confirmed on RTX 3090 (JAX 0.6.0) in #37181.

**Kind of Contribution**
Bug Fix

**Benchmark**
N/A — this is a correctness fix, not a performance change. The original `=1` override was added for "float-division heavy benchmarks" but `div.full` trades correctness for speed; `div.rnd` is LLVM's default and is IEEE-754 compliant with >1 ULP accuracy.

**Unit Tests**
New regression test: `xla/tests/ieee_f32_division_test.cc` (registered as `//xla/tests:ieee_f32_division_test`, runs on cpu+gpu) asserts the IEEE-754 identity properties `x / x == 1.0` and `x / 1.0 == x` that the `div.full` override broke, across values including `FLT_MAX`, `FLT_MIN`, `1e10`, `1e-10`. It uses parameters and disabled fast math so the division is actually executed by the backend rather than folded or simplified away. Existing GPU backend tests continue to pass: `nvptx_backend_test`, `load_ir_module_test`, `utils_test`, `nvptx_utils_test`.

**Execution Tests**
A standalone reproducer script is available at `repro_xla_37181.py` that verifies IEEE-754 division compliance across 5 categories (identity, inverse, overflow, underflow, NaN).

display_title: [XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate U64 key packing/unpacking and RAFT max_k heuristic in TopkSpecializer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate U64 key packing/unpacking and RAFT max_k heuristic in TopkSpecializer.

- `BuildPackF32ToU64TotalOrder` and `BuildPackF32ToU64PartialOrder` shared the same F32-to-U32 bitwise radix flip and U64 packing logic, differing only in the reversed index bound (`0xFFFFFFFF` for `kTotal` vs. `0x7FFFFFFF` for `kPartial`) and the `-0.0f` canonicalization step for `kPartial` (shifting the 31-bit reversed index left by 1, adding `is_neg_zero` to `radix_key`, and storing `is_neg_zero` in bit 0).
- `BuildUnpackU64ToF32TotalOrder` and `BuildUnpackU64ToF32PartialOrder` were identical except that `kPartial` subtracts bit 0 (`is_neg_zero`) from the extracted upper 32-bit key before unflipping. Also use `BroadcastU32` for the shift constant `31` instead of constructing the constant and broadcast manually.
- The `F32`/`BF16` `max_k` upper-bound calculation for RAFT `select_k` in `ShouldRewriteStableTopKToUint64` and `SmallBufferOptimization` was identical (with `SmallBufferOptimization` also setting `min_n = 1`).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator binary and ternary elementwise setup.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator binary and ternary elementwise setup.

`HloEvaluatorTypedVisitor<ReturnT, ElementwiseT>` is instantiated across 32 primitive types, duplicating shape/layout validation, operand `Literal` lookup, result `Literal` allocation, and `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` move/teardown across binary and ternary `Handle*` instantiations.

```
// Before (duplicated per type T and per binary/ternary Handle* opcode):
HandleOp(hlo): ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(Literal lit, ElementWiseBinaryOp(hlo, fn));
               parent_->SetEvaluatedLiteralFor(hlo, std::move(lit));

// After (shared non-template setup/storage; typed inner loop captured by value):
HandleOp(hlo): return ElementWiseBinaryOp(hlo, fn);  // -> RunElementwiseBinaryOp(...)
```

Specifically:
- Factor type-independent shape/scalar checks, operand lookup, `Literal(shape)` allocation, and `SetEvaluatedLiteralFor` storage into non-template `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseBinaryOp` and `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseTernaryOp` helpers in `xla/hlo/evaluator/hlo_evaluator.cc`, returning `absl::Status` directly and dropping redundant `<ReturnT, ReturnT, ReturnT>` template parameters on `ElementwiseTernaryOp`.
- Capture raw operand data pointers, scalar flags, and `absl::FunctionRef`s by value in `ElementWiseBinaryOpImpl` and `ElementwiseTernaryOpImpl`'s `PopulateLinearParallel` / `PopulateParallel` lambdas (instead of `[&]` captures and `ConvertBinaryFunction`'s `[&]` wrapper), eliminating 3 pointer-chasing memory loads per element inside `MutableLiteralBase::PopulateLinearInplaceInternal`'s type-erased `FunctionRef` callback.

**Runtime & Memory Performance Impact:**
- **CPU:** Improves `BM_BinaryOp/512` by 7.74% and `BM_BinaryOp/1024` by 9.68% (`p=0.000`, 20-run `-c opt --config=benchmark`) in `//xla/hlo/evaluator:hlo_evaluator_test`, because storing `lhs_data`, `rhs_data`, and `binary_op` inline in the `PopulateLinearParallel` lambda removes 3 pointer-dereference loads per element across the per-element indirect callback (`20 -> 17` instructions/element for `F32` `add`).
- **Memory:** Heap allocations are unchanged (`Literal(shape)` is allocated once and moved directly into `EvaluationState`), and per-op stack usage shrinks by removing intermediate `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` return frames.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007265841

display_title: Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

head_commit.message:
Add CPU kernels for lgamma and digamma.

Previously, `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` were lowered as large graphs of primitive operations, which made both compilation and execution slow.

This change replaces the CPU implementation of `lax.lgamma` and `lax.digamma` with C++ kernels in a new `_math` extension, vectorized with Highway and parallelized across threads for large arrays. Both kernels keep the same accuracy bounds (`<= 1.0` ULP for `float16`/`float32`/`float64` and `<= 0.5` ULP for `bfloat16`), support sharded execution and `jax.export`, and fix batch partitioning for custom calls when all dimensions are batch dimensions.

display_title: PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

head_commit.message:
PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48501

First of three PRs that add `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` support to the ROCm tracer: this PR, #48502 (the parser) and #48503 (the wiring). This one is groundwork and adds no new options.

- Move `RocmTracerOptions` from `rocm_tracer.h` to `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, which has no ROCm dependency, so host-only targets (the parser in #48502) can use it. `rocm_tracer.h` already includes `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, so existing code is unaffected.
- Replace `AnnotationMap::Clear()` with `Reset(max_annotation_strings)`, which clears the entries and sets the capacity under one lock. The capacity was a `const` 1M. `RocmTracer::Enable()` calls `Reset()` before it starts the rocprofiler context.
- `AnnotationMap::Add()` checks the capacity once per event, so an event's annotation, ROCTX range and scope range ID are stored together or not at all. Before, the event that filled the last slot kept its annotation but lost its scope range ID.
- `RocmTracerOptions::max_annotation_strings` is a `std::optional` with no default. `Enable()` returns `InvalidArgument` if it is unset; 0 retains nothing.
- `RocmTraceCollectorOptions` fields default to 0 instead of being indeterminate, and its `max_annotation_strings`, which was set but never read, is removed.
- `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` drops its unused `//xla/service:gpu_plugin` dep, which `dwyu` flags once this PR edits the target's source, and depends on `rocm_tracer_utils` directly. `HloOpProfiler` takes an injected runner, and every binary that links it gets the plugin through `xla_test` or `matmul_perf_table_gen`, so link inputs don't change. `hlo_op_profiler_cuda` and `hlo_op_profiler_stub` still list it and can be cleaned up separately.

**Behaviour change:** `GpuTracer` sessions now get the 4M annotation capacity that `GetRocmTracerOptions()` already requested; `Enable()` ignored it and used 1M. display_title: [XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

When an operand of `tt.expand_dims` already contains a unit dimension adjacent
to the expanded axis, `triton_xla.squeeze_dims` on the pre-existing unit axis
produces the same tensor type as the `tt.expand_dims` operand. Checking type
equality instead of axis equality cancels the two ops instead of swapping them,
which stops `squeeze_dims` from reaching upstream `xtile.extract` tiles and
drops the `tt.expand_dims` before `tt.broadcast`.

Only fold `squeeze_dims(expand_dims(x))` to `x` when the axes match or `x` is a
1D unit tensor that cannot be squeezed further; otherwise swap the two ops so
unit dimensions continue propagating upward.

display_title: PR #50069: [ROCm] Fall back to an unfused FP8 conversion when hipBLASLt has no kernel

head_commit.message:
PR #50069: [ROCm] Fall back to an unfused FP8 conversion when hipBLASLt has no kernel

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50069

## Motivation

hipBLASLt's kernel coverage for FP8 outputs differs between GPUs and library releases. Today an FP8-output GEMM that hipBLASLt has no algorithm for fails to compile with "No supported configs found". This adds an autotuner fallback that runs it with a wider output and converts to FP8 separately.

Part of a series: depends on #50068, which adds `GemmBackendConfig.has_d_scale` (its commit is included here until it lands). Independent of #49829, the FP8 output fusion on ROCm.

## Details

- When hipBLASLt returns no algorithm for an FP8-output `__cublas$lt$matmul$f8`, `HipblasLtBackend` offers the algorithms of a wider-output copy, marked by a new `GemmKey.unfuse_fp8_output`. `ApplyConfig` rewrites the call into that GEMM plus a loop fusion for the D scale, saturating clamp and conversion.
- The fallback is offered only when the fused query is empty, so fused kernels are never displaced. `HIPBLASLT_FISSION` gets it through its inner backend, and cached or AOT results replay it without a device.
- It logs a warning when it fires, like the MX path.
- Limitation: deviceless/AOT compiles without autotune results can't query hipBLASLt, so a missing kernel there still fails at run time.

## Test Plan

On gfx950, ran `hipblaslt_test` (fallback offered only without fused algorithms, including a D-scaled mixed-input GEMM, plus the rewrite) and `gemm_rewriter_fp8_test` (forced fallback for an FP8 dot, executed against the reference), along with the other ROCm GEMM tests.

## Test Result

All pass on gfx950.

display_title: [XLA] Add unified AI agent PR preparation guidelines in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add unified AI agent PR preparation guidelines in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md.

**Status quo**
The root `AGENTS.md` in `openxla/xla` contains only a short pointer to `xla/AGENTS.md`, and the repository root lacks `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` files. Meanwhile, OpenXLA team members maintain separate review, readability, compatibility, and PR preparation skills covering C++17 constraints, `#ifdef` avoidance, GPU AOT compatibility, CUDA runtime version checks, CPU ABI stability, compiler phase invariants, and unit testing standards.

**Why**
Contributors use different AI coding assistants (OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, and Gemini CLI) to author and prepare XLA Pull Requests. Providing a single, identical, comprehensive instruction set across `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `GEMINI.md` in the OpenXLA root ensures every agent applies the team's review and PR preparation standards before a PR is opened.

**Design choices**
- Aggregate the OpenXLA team's review, readability, compiler architecture, compatibility, and testing skills into `third_party/xla/AGENTS.md`.
- Replicate the exact same content into `third_party/xla/CLAUDE.md` and `third_party/xla/GEMINI.md` so all three files remain byte-for-byte identical.
- Register `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` in `_XLA_TOP_LEVEL_FILES` in `third_party/xla/common.bara.sky` so Copybara exports all three files to the root of `openxla/xla`.

**Compromises**
- Keeping `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and `GEMINI.md` as three identical files introduces file duplication at the repository root, because GitHub and agent CLIs do not universally follow symlinks or cross-file include directives across tools.

**Alternatives**
- Symlinking `CLAUDE.md` and `GEMINI.md` to `AGENTS.md` was rejected because Copybara and several agent CLIs expect regular files rather than symlinks.

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, and rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated).
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kReduce and kReduceWindow in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Check that the output subshape and corresponding `to_apply` parameter types of `kReduce` and `kReduceWindow`, as well as any `kConvert` instructions in their `to_apply` subcomputation, have a precision-preserving element type transition relative to the reduced operand (`in_type == out_type` or between `high_precision_type_` and `low_precision_type_`).

Combined with the `kConvert` check in `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision`, this prevents `BFloat16Propagation` from propagating `BF16` through `kReduce` or `kReduceWindow` when the `to_apply` subcomputation narrows or truncates values (either via `kConvert`, such as `F32 -> S32 -> F32` or `F32 -> F16 -> F32`, or implicitly via mixed-precision parameter/output types), while still allowing same-type converts, conversions between `high_precision_type_` and `low_precision_type_`, and non-`kConvert` instructions of other element types (such as `PRED` predicates or `S32` variadic branches).

head_commit.message:
PR #48501: [ROCm] Add  `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` into the ROCm tracer (PR1)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48501

First of three PRs that add `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration` support to the ROCm tracer: this PR, #48502 (the parser) and #48503 (the wiring). This one is groundwork and adds no new options.

- Move `RocmTracerOptions` from `rocm_tracer.h` to `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, which has no ROCm dependency, so host-only targets (the parser in #48502) can use it. `rocm_tracer.h` already includes `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, so existing code is unaffected.
- Replace `AnnotationMap::Clear()` with `Reset(max_annotation_strings)`, which clears the entries and sets the capacity under one lock. The capacity was a `const` 1M. `RocmTracer::Enable()` calls `Reset()` before it starts the rocprofiler context.
- `AnnotationMap::Add()` checks the capacity once per event, so an event's annotation, ROCTX range and scope range ID are stored together or not at all. Before, the event that filled the last slot kept its annotation but lost its scope range ID.
- `RocmTracerOptions::max_annotation_strings` is a `std::optional` with no default. `Enable()` returns `InvalidArgument` if it is unset; 0 retains nothing.
- `RocmTraceCollectorOptions` fields default to 0 instead of being indeterminate, and its `max_annotation_strings`, which was set but never read, is removed.
- `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` drops its unused `//xla/service:gpu_plugin` dep, which `dwyu` flags once this PR edits the target's source, and depends on `rocm_tracer_utils` directly. `HloOpProfiler` takes an injected runner, and every binary that links it gets the plugin through `xla_test` or `matmul_perf_table_gen`, so link inputs don't change. `hlo_op_profiler_cuda` and `hlo_op_profiler_stub` still list it and can be cleaned up separately.

**Behaviour change:** `GpuTracer` sessions now get the 4M annotation capacity that `GetRocmTracerOptions()` already requested; `Enable()` ignored it and used 1M. The cap counts distinct strings, so most workloads won't see a difference (CUPTI's default is 1M). `hlo_op_profiler_rocm` keeps 1M. #48502 adds `gpu_max_annotation_strings` to set another value.

🎯 Justification

The ROCm `GpuTracer` ignores `advanced_configuration`: it reads only `device_type()`, so any `gpu_*` key a user sets, or misspells, is silently dropped. The CUPTI backend parses the map, but a bad key fails `Start()`, and `ProfilerController` then skips `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace with only a log line. #48502 and #48503 instead report problems in `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and keep tracing. They need `RocmTracerOptions` in a header without ROCm dependencies, and an annotation capacity that can be set per session; this PR provides both.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

♻️ Cleanup, 🐛 Bug Fix

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

In `GpuAliasInfo`, a fused keys-only `sort` has an array output shape (`user_index == {}`), so comparing `user_index` against `ShapeIndex{0}` always rejected in-place buffer sharing. Only compare against the operand index when the `sort` output is a tuple, and require `user_index.empty()` otherwise.

display_title: [XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator binary and ternary elementwise setup.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator binary and ternary elementwise setup.

`HloEvaluatorTypedVisitor<ReturnT, ElementwiseT>` is instantiated across 32 primitive types, duplicating shape/layout validation, operand `Literal` lookup, result `Literal` allocation, and `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` move/teardown across binary and ternary `Handle*` instantiations.

```
// Before (duplicated per type T and per binary/ternary Handle* opcode):
HandleOp(hlo): ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(Literal lit, ElementWiseBinaryOp(hlo, fn));
               parent_->SetEvaluatedLiteralFor(hlo, std::move(lit));

// After (shared non-template setup/storage; typed inner loop captured by value):
HandleOp(hlo): return ElementWiseBinaryOp(hlo, fn);  // -> RunElementwiseBinaryOp(...)
```

Specifically:
- Factor type-independent shape/scalar checks, operand lookup, `Literal(shape)` allocation, and `SetEvaluatedLiteralFor` storage into non-template `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseBinaryOp` and `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseTernaryOp` helpers in `xla/hlo/evaluator/hlo_evaluator.cc`, returning `absl::Status` directly and dropping redundant `<ReturnT, ReturnT, ReturnT>` template parameters on `ElementwiseTernaryOp`.
- Capture raw operand data pointers, scalar flags, and `absl::FunctionRef`s by value in `ElementWiseBinaryOpImpl` and `ElementwiseTernaryOpImpl`'s `PopulateLinearParallel` / `PopulateParallel` lambdas (instead of `[&]` captures and `ConvertBinaryFunction`'s `[&]` wrapper), eliminating 3 pointer-chasing memory loads per element inside `MutableLiteralBase::PopulateLinearInplaceInternal`'s type-erased `FunctionRef` callback.

**Runtime & Memory Performance Impact:**
- **CPU:** Improves `BM_BinaryOp/512` by 7.74% and `BM_BinaryOp/1024` by 9.68% (`p=0.000`, 20-run `-c opt --config=benchmark`) in `//xla/hlo/evaluator:hlo_evaluator_test`, because storing `lhs_data`, `rhs_data`, and `binary_op` inline in the `PopulateLinearParallel` lambda removes 3 pointer-dereference loads per element across the per-element indirect callback (`20 -> 17` instructions/element for `F32` `add`).
- **Memory:** Heap allocations are unchanged (`Literal(shape)` is allocated once and moved directly into `EvaluationState`), and per-op stack usage shrinks by removing intermediate `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` return frames.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1006517108

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

When an operand of `tt.expand_dims` already contains a unit dimension adjacent
to the expanded axis, `triton_xla.squeeze_dims` on the pre-existing unit axis
produces the same tensor type as the `tt.expand_dims` operand. Checking type
equality instead of axis equality cancels the two ops instead of swapping them,
which stops `squeeze_dims` from reaching upstream `xtile.extract` tiles and
drops the `tt.expand_dims` before `tt.broadcast`.

Only fold `squeeze_dims(expand_dims(x))` to `x` when the axes match or `x` is a
1D unit tensor that cannot be squeezed further; otherwise swap the two ops so
unit dimensions continue propagating upward.

display_title: [XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator unary op setup and dead handlers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator unary op setup and dead handlers.

`HloEvaluatorTypedVisitor<ReturnT, ElementwiseT>` is instantiated across 32 primitive types, duplicating shape/layout validation, operand `Literal` lookup, result `Literal` allocation, and `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` move/teardown across unary `Handle*` instantiations, while also instantiating 26 floating-point/complex unary handlers on `bool` and 14 integer types via C++11 `<cmath>` integral overloads (`double std::sin(Integral)`, etc.) that upstream `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape` / `HloVerifier` already reject.

```
// Before (duplicated per type T and per unary Handle* opcode):
HandleOp(hlo): ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(Literal lit, ElementWiseUnaryOp(hlo, fn));
               parent_->SetEvaluatedLiteralFor(hlo, std::move(lit));

// After (shared non-template setup/storage; typed inner loop captured by value):
HandleOp(hlo): if constexpr (valid_for_ElementwiseT)  // for 26 FP/complex ops
                 return ElementWiseUnaryOp(hlo, fn);  // -> RunElementwiseUnaryOp(...)
```

Specifically:
- Factor type-independent shape checks, operand lookup, `Literal(shape)` allocation, and `SetEvaluatedLiteralFor` storage into non-template `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseUnaryOp` in `xla/hlo/evaluator/hlo_evaluator.cc`, returning `absl::Status` directly from `ElementWiseUnaryOp` / `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl`.
- Capture `operand_data` and `unary_op` (`absl::FunctionRef`) by value in `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl`'s `PopulateLinearParallel` / `PopulateParallel` lambdas instead of wrapping via `ConvertUnaryFunction`'s `[&]` lambda, eliminating 3 pointer-chasing memory loads per element inside `MutableLiteralBase::PopulateLinearInplaceInternal`'s type-erased `FunctionRef` callback.
- Guard the 26 floating-point and floating-or-complex unary handlers (`HandleSin`, `HandleCos`, `HandleExp`, `HandleRound`, `HandleFloor`, `HandleCeil`, etc.) with `if constexpr` on `ElementwiseT` matching `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape`, avoiding dead elementwise loop instantiations across the 15 `PRED`/integral visitors and returning `UnsupportedTypeError` if an unverified instruction reaches `HloEvaluator`.

**Runtime & Memory Performance Impact:**
- **CPU:** Improves `BM_UnaryOp/512` by 6.97% and `BM_UnaryOp/1024` by 6.68% (`p=0.000`, 20-run `-c opt --config=benchmark`) in `//xla/hlo/evaluator:hlo_evaluator_test`, because storing `operand_data` and `unary_op` inline in the `PopulateLinearParallel` lambda removes 3 pointer-dereference loads per element across the per-element indirect callback (`18 -> 15` instructions/element for `F32` `exp`).
- **Memory:** Heap allocations are unchanged (`Literal(shape)` is allocated once and moved directly into `EvaluationState`), and per-op stack usage drops from 768 B to 32 B in `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl` by removing intermediate `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` stack frames.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007235884

display_title: [XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate U64 key packing/unpacking and RAFT max_k heuristic in TopkSpecializer.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate U64 key packing/unpacking and RAFT max_k heuristic in TopkSpecializer.

- `BuildPackF32ToU64TotalOrder` and `BuildPackF32ToU64PartialOrder` shared the same F32-to-U32 bitwise radix flip and U64 packing logic, differing only in the reversed index bound (`0xFFFFFFFF` for `kTotal` vs. `0x7FFFFFFF` for `kPartial`) and the `-0.0f` canonicalization step for `kPartial` (shifting the 31-bit reversed index left by 1, adding `is_neg_zero` to `radix_key`, and storing `is_neg_zero` in bit 0).
- `BuildUnpackU64ToF32TotalOrder` and `BuildUnpackU64ToF32PartialOrder` were identical except that `kPartial` subtracts bit 0 (`is_neg_zero`) from the extracted upper 32-bit key before unflipping. Also use `BroadcastU32` for the shift constant `31` instead of constructing the constant and broadcast manually.
- The `F32`/`BF16` `max_k` upper-bound calculation for RAFT `select_k` in `ShouldRewriteStableTopKToUint64` and `SmallBufferOptimization` was identical (with `SmallBufferOptimization` also setting `min_n = 1`).

head_commit.message:
Propagate BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto through CublasLtBackend autotuner

Previously `AutotuneResult::GemmKey` and `GemmBackendConfig` only recorded the heuristic algorithm index for cuBLASLt GEMMs.

This change adds an optional `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` field to `AutotuneResult::GemmKey` and `GemmBackendConfig` and updates `CublasLtBackend` to populate and apply the algorithm descriptor proto during autotuning. This way the selected cuBLASLt algorithm configuration is preserved in the HLO backend config instead of relying solely on the heuristic index.

display_title: Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff CI runs

head_commit.message:
Exclude manual targets in bazel-diff CI runs

When `bazel-diff` selects impacted targets, `xla/build_tools/ci/build.py` passes explicit target labels via `--target_pattern_file`. Unlike wildcard patterns (`//xla/...` and `@tsl//tsl/...`), explicit labels in `--target_pattern_file` ignore `tags = ["manual"]`, causing manual tests such as `@tsl//tsl/platform:numa_test` to run and fail on CI runners.

So this change appends `-manual` to `--build_tag_filters` and `--test_tag_filters` whenever `target_pattern_file` is set (matching `xla/build_tools/rocm/run_xla_ci_build.sh`), and caps the impacted targets list rendered to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` in `xla/build_tools/ci/bazel_diff.py` at 500 entries so large diffs stay below GitHub's 1024 KB step summary limit.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007224916

display_title: Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

head_commit.message:
Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

Heuristic indices returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` depend on the GPU and cuBLASLt version, so the same index can resolve to a different kernel across devices or library updates.

Therefore this change introduces `CublasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` (along with their proto definitions in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cublas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto` and `xla/stream_executor/gpu/blas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto`) to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` implements `GetBlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `GetMatmulAlgorithm` to extract and reconstruct `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptors, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` and `BlasLt::GetOrCreateMatmulPlanWithAlgorithm` add overloads accepting `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm`.

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

With the VMM allocator, pinned_host buffers got device memory with no
CPU mapping, so any CPU access segfaulted (orbax checkpoint saves, for
example). Command buffer update modes other than ALWAYS_UPDATE force
the VMM allocator, so they were affected too.

The PJRT GPU client now passes the VMM allocator the same pinned host
allocators the BFC path uses, through the generic
DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create() with no CUDA/ROCm #if branches.
Without a host allocator, MemorySpace::kHost now fails with

display_title: PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

head_commit.message:
PR #51053: Fix NULL pointer dereference in HloEvaluator when evaluating a literal-less kConstant instruction

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/51053

## Summary / Root Cause
`HloInstruction::CreateFromProto` (xla/hlo/ir/hlo_instruction.cc) constructs
a literal-less `HloConstantInstruction` whenever a `kConstant`
`HloInstructionProto` has no `literal` field set — regardless of the
`prohibit_empty_literal` parameter, which currently only governs an
*existing-but-empty* literal, not an *entirely absent* one. This state is
meant only for tooling that intentionally drops an oversized constant's
literal when dumping a module (`HloConstantInstruction::HasLiteral()` /
`DropLiteral()`).

If such a module is later evaluated, it crashes:
`HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()` unconditionally calls
`HloInstruction::literal()` whenever `IsConstant()` is true, which
dereferences the null `literal_` (`std::shared_ptr<Literal>`), producing a
SIGSEGV.

Found via a libFuzzer + ASan/UBSan harness targeting the
`HloModuleProto` deserialize → `HloEvaluator::Evaluate` path. Minimal
trigger: a single `kConstant` instruction proto with no `literal` field.

## The Fix

1. `HloInstruction::CreateFromProto`: when a `kConstant` proto has no
   `literal` and `prohibit_empty_literal` is true (the default used by
   every evaluation-facing caller — `run_hlo_module`, PJRT executable
   loading, etc.), return `absl::InvalidArgumentError` instead of silently
   constructing a literal-less instruction. This resolves the existing
   `TODO(b/110214922)`. Callers that genuinely need the "literal dropped"
   dump-only representation can still get it by passing
   `prohibit_empty_literal=false`.
2. `HloEvaluator::GetEvaluatedLiteralFor()`: added a `CHECK(HasLiteral())`
   defense-in-depth guard, consistent with the existing
   `CHECK(literal != nullptr)` a few lines below it, so that if any other
   path ever constructs a literal-less constant, evaluation fails with a
   clear diagnostic instead of a raw null-pointer SEGV.

## Impact

Prevents a denial-of-service crash (CWE-476, null pointer dereference) when
evaluating a malformed or maliciously crafted `HloModuleProto` whose
constant instruction is missing its literal payload. This affects any
consumer that deserializes and evaluates/interprets an `HloModuleProto` not
produced by XLA's own trusted compilation pipeline (the HLO interpreter
backend, `run_hlo_module`, or constant-folding over a less-trusted module).

## Behavior change to note for reviewers

Any existing caller that loads a "literal-dropped" dump **with**
`prohibit_empty_literal=true` and only inspects structure/shapes (never
evaluates) will now get an error instead of a literal-less instruction. That
matches the flag's documented intent ("prohibit empty literal") and we
believe no in-tree caller relies on the previous silent-success behavior for
this exact combination, but flagging it explicitly since it's the one
observable behavior change.

display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, and rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated).
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

display_title: Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

In `GpuAliasInfo`, a fused keys-only `sort` has an array output shape (`user_index == {}`), so comparing `user_index` against `ShapeIndex{0}` always rejected in-place buffer sharing. Only compare against the operand index when the `sort` output is a tuple, and require `user_index.empty()` otherwise.

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005841220

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU][NFC] Deduplicate U64 key packing/unpacking and RAFT max_k heuristic in TopkSpecializer.

- `BuildPackF32ToU64TotalOrder` and `BuildPackF32ToU64PartialOrder` shared the same F32-to-U32 bitwise radix flip and U64 packing logic, differing only in the reversed index bound (`0xFFFFFFFF` for `kTotal` vs. `0x7FFFFFFF` for `kPartial`) and the `-0.0f` canonicalization step for `kPartial` (shifting the 31-bit reversed index left by 1, adding `is_neg_zero` to `radix_key`, and storing `is_neg_zero` in bit 0).
- `BuildUnpackU64ToF32TotalOrder` and `BuildUnpackU64ToF32PartialOrder` were identical except that `kPartial` subtracts bit 0 (`is_neg_zero`) from the extracted upper 32-bit key before unflipping. Also use `BroadcastU32` for the shift constant `31` instead of constructing the constant and broadcast manually.
- The `F32`/`BF16` `max_k` upper-bound calculation for RAFT `select_k` in `ShouldRewriteStableTopKToUint64` and `SmallBufferOptimization` was identical (with `SmallBufferOptimization` also setting `min_n = 1`).

display_title: [XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator unary op setup and dead handlers.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Deduplicate HloEvaluator unary op setup and dead handlers.

`HloEvaluatorTypedVisitor<ReturnT, ElementwiseT>` is instantiated across 32 primitive types, duplicating shape/layout validation, operand `Literal` lookup, result `Literal` allocation, and `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` move/teardown across unary `Handle*` instantiations, while also instantiating 26 floating-point/complex unary handlers on `bool` and 14 integer types via C++11 `<cmath>` integral overloads (`double std::sin(Integral)`, etc.) that upstream `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape` / `HloVerifier` already reject.

```
// Before (duplicated per type T and per unary Handle* opcode):
HandleOp(hlo): ASSIGN_OR_RETURN(Literal lit, ElementWiseUnaryOp(hlo, fn));
               parent_->SetEvaluatedLiteralFor(hlo, std::move(lit));

// After (shared non-template setup/storage; typed inner loop captured by value):
HandleOp(hlo): if constexpr (valid_for_ElementwiseT)  // for 26 FP/complex ops
                 return ElementWiseUnaryOp(hlo, fn);  // -> RunElementwiseUnaryOp(...)
```

Specifically:
- Factor type-independent shape checks, operand lookup, `Literal(shape)` allocation, and `SetEvaluatedLiteralFor` storage into non-template `HloEvaluator::RunElementwiseUnaryOp` in `xla/hlo/evaluator/hlo_evaluator.cc`, returning `absl::Status` directly from `ElementWiseUnaryOp` / `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl`.
- Capture `operand_data` and `unary_op` (`absl::FunctionRef`) by value in `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl`'s `PopulateLinearParallel` / `PopulateParallel` lambdas instead of wrapping via `ConvertUnaryFunction`'s `[&]` lambda, eliminating 3 pointer-chasing memory loads per element inside `MutableLiteralBase::PopulateLinearInplaceInternal`'s type-erased `FunctionRef` callback.
- Guard the 26 floating-point and floating-or-complex unary handlers (`HandleSin`, `HandleCos`, `HandleExp`, `HandleRound`, `HandleFloor`, `HandleCeil`, etc.) with `if constexpr` on `ElementwiseT` matching `ShapeInference::InferUnaryOpShape`, avoiding dead elementwise loop instantiations across the 15 `PRED`/integral visitors and returning `UnsupportedTypeError` if an unverified instruction reaches `HloEvaluator`.

**Runtime & Memory Performance Impact:**
- **CPU:** Improves `BM_UnaryOp/512` by 6.97% and `BM_UnaryOp/1024` by 6.68% (`p=0.000`, 20-run `-c opt --config=benchmark`) in `//xla/hlo/evaluator:hlo_evaluator_test`, because storing `operand_data` and `unary_op` inline in the `PopulateLinearParallel` lambda removes 3 pointer-dereference loads per element across the per-element indirect callback (`18 -> 15` instructions/element for `F32` `exp`).
- **Memory:** Heap allocations are unchanged (`Literal(shape)` is allocated once and moved directly into `EvaluationState`), and per-op stack usage drops from 768 B to 32 B in `ElementWiseUnaryOpImpl` by removing intermediate `absl::StatusOr<Literal>` stack frames.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: **Status quo**

head_commit.message:
**Status quo**
`CudnnScaledDotHelper::IsSupported` requires both `lhs` and `rhs` contracting dimensions of `kScaledDot` to be the minor dimension (`rank - 1`, i.e., `NT` layout), and `GpuLayoutAssignment` assigns the default `{1, 0}` layout to all four `kScaledDot` operands. When `lhs` or `rhs` has contracting dimension `0` (`NN`, `TN`, or `TT`), `NVPTXCompiler::IsScaledDotSupportedByBackend` rejects the instruction during `ScaledDotRewriter`, decomposing `kScaledDot` into an upcast and BF16 `dot`.

**Why**
Falling back to decomposed BF16 `dot` on `NN`, `TN`, and `TT` loses 1.5x to 5.0x throughput on Blackwell B200 compared to native cuDNN block-scaled GEMM (`__cudnn$fusion`). Both fixed `{1, 0}` entry parameter layouts and unconstrained `AUTO` entry parameter layouts need to lower to `__cudnn$fusion` across `MXFP8`, `MXFP4`, and `NVFP4`.

**Design choices**
- Relax pre-fusion `CudnnScaledDotHelper::IsSupported(scaled_dot, /*is_fused=*/false)` in `NVPTXCompiler::IsScaledDotSupportedByBackend` so `ScaledDotRewriter` preserves `NN`, `TN`, and `TT` `kScaledDot` instructions before layout assignment.
- Add `GpuLayoutAssignment::AddScaledDotBackendConstraints` to set minor-contracting layouts on `lhs`, `rhs`, `lhs_scale`, and `rhs_scale` via `SetDotOperandLayoutToMinorContracting` when `!xla_gpu_experimental_scaled_dot_with_triton()`. For `AUTO` entry layouts, `{0, 1}` propagates to entry parameters with zero runtime data transposes; for fixed `{1, 0}` entry layouts, `LayoutAssignment` inserts `kCopy` to `{0, 1}`.
- Add `LayoutNormalization::HandleScaledDot` to absorb non-default-layout `kBitcast` operands and update `dot_dimension_numbers()` so both contracting dimensions become `rank - 1` (`NT`) before `SubByteNormalization`.
- Prevent `GemmFusion` from fusing `kTranspose` into `kScaledDot` fusions when `!xla_gpu_experimental_scaled_dot_with_triton()`, keeping `kScaledDot` operands as fusion parameters.
- Add `UnwrapScaleTranspose` in `CudnnScaledDotHelper::AddScaleSwizzle` to fold any preceding 2D/3D scale `kTranspose` directly into the 6D scale swizzle (`dimensions={0, 3, 1, 5, 4, 2}` instead of `{0, 1, 4, 3, 2, 5}`), avoiding a separate scale transpose kernel.
- Update `cudnn_scaled_dot_test` to expect `kSupported` on all 24 `MXFP8`, `MXFP4`, and `NVFP4` rows, add an `AUTO` entry layout test, and add the B200 benchmark and backend-verification suite.

**Compromises**
- When entry parameters have a fixed `{1, 0}` layout with major contracting dimension, `lhs` and/or `rhs` data tensors still require an explicit runtime transpose kernel before `__cudnn$fusion` because cuDNN's `BlockScaleDequantizeNode` requires unit stride on the contracting dimension.

**Alternatives**
- Relaxing contracting-dimension constraints inside `CuDnnFusionCompiler` without transposing data operands in advance fails during `CuDnnFusionCompiler::GetAvailablePlanCount` because cuDNN rejects non-unit contracting strides on block-scaled inputs.
- Canonicalizing `kScaledDot` only after `GpuLayoutAssignment` (in `BlockScalingRewriter`) works for fixed `{1, 0}` entry layouts, but misses zero-copy layout propagation when entry parameter layouts are `AUTO`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007204309

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

display_title: PR #50683: [XLA:GPU] Set max_total_seq_len for packed cuDNN flash attention backward

head_commit.message:
PR #50683: [XLA:GPU] Set max_total_seq_len for packed cuDNN flash attention backward

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50683

📝 Summary of Changes

`GetCudnnFlashAttentionBackwardOperationGraph` now tells cuDNN the maximum packed token count for packed (ragged) SDPA backward. When `max_seg_per_batch` > 1, it computes `max_total_seq_len_q = B * S_q` and `max_total_seq_len_kv = B * S_kv`. It passes them to the graph via `set_max_total_seq_len_q` and `set_max_total_seq_len_kv`. Dense and padding-only graphs are unchanged.

🎯 Justification

For packed graphs, Q/K/V/dO/O/dQ/dK/dV are declared as shape `[B, H, S, D]` with additional attribute `max_seg_per_batch` in XLA to indicate how many segments are packed inside each batch. Without this setting, cuDNN sizes the backward workspace for `B * max_seg_per_batch * S` tokens. The real token count cannot exceed `B * S`, because each of the B physical rows holds at most S tokens. The two dominant workspace terms, `softmax_sum` and the FP32 `dQ_accum`, scale with this token count and shrink by a factor of `max_seg_per_batch`.

Workloads that benefit: packed or segmented-sequence attention training, such as JAX/Flax/MaxText with `max_segments_per_batch` > 1, where backward workspace is often the peak-memory driver.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

⚡️ Performance Improvement

head_commit.message:
Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

Heuristic indices returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` depend on the GPU and cuBLASLt version, so the same index can resolve to a different kernel across devices or library updates.

Therefore this change introduces `CublasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` (along with their proto definitions in `xla/stream_executor/cuda/cublas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto` and `xla/stream_executor/gpu/blas_lt_matmul_algorithm.proto`) to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` implements `GetBlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `GetMatmulAlgorithm` to extract and reconstruct `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptors, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` and `BlasLt::GetOrCreateMatmulPlanWithAlgorithm` add overloads accepting `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm`.

display_title: Set unique collective op_id on CPU and compute per-call Gloo tags.

head_commit.message:
Set unique collective op_id on CPU and compute per-call Gloo tags.

Previously, `ThunkEmitter` set `op_id` on every collective thunk to `channel_id` when present or to the module ID otherwise, and `GlooCommunicator` hardcoded `tag = 0` on all collective operations. While the presence of `channel_id` (`has_channel_id`) still selects the collective group mode (such as `CROSS_PARTITION` or `FLATTENED_ID`), its numeric value was originally meant for matching collectives across separate modules in MPMD programs. In modern single-module SPMD programs, passes often set a constant dummy `channel_id` (such as `1`) just to mark `has_channel_id = true`, which gave multiple collectives in the same module the same `op_id`.

Update `GetCollectiveOpParams` in `xla/service/cpu/thunk_emitter.cc` to set `op_id` to `instruction->unique_id()`, giving each collective instruction in a module a distinct static ID while preserving `has_channel_id` for group-mode selection. In `xla/backends/cpu/collectives/gloo_communicator.cc`, track a per-`op_id` loop counter for the active `RunId` and fingerprint `(op_id, run_id, loop_counter)` into Gloo's 32-bit tag for `AllReduce`, `CollectivePermute`, `AllToAll`, `AllGather`, and `ReduceScatter`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1000509791

[XLA:GPU] Swap different-axis squeeze_dims and expand_dims in Triton

When an operand of `tt.expand_dims` already contains a unit dimension adjacent
to the expanded axis, `triton_xla.squeeze_dims` on the pre-existing unit axis
produces the same tensor type as the `tt.expand_dims` operand. Checking type
equality instead of axis equality cancels the two ops instead of swapping them,
which stops `squeeze_dims` from reaching upstream `xtile.extract` tiles and
drops the `tt.expand_dims` before `tt.broadcast`.

Only fold `squeeze_dims(expand_dims(x))` to `x` when the axes match or `x` is a
1D unit tensor that cannot be squeezed further; otherwise swap the two ops so
unit dimensions continue propagating upward.
