display_title: PR #50225: [XLA:GPU] Support multi-output fusion in the concatenate emitter

head_commit.message:
PR #50225: [XLA:GPU] Support multi-output fusion in the concatenate emitter

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50225

📝 Summary of Changes
- The concatenate emitter emits fusions with several roots. Each distinct hero is computed once per operand loop, and one shared epilogue writes all outputs.
- UseConcatenateFusion accepts several roots when the heroes are concatenates with identical splits, the roots share one shape, and roots × operands ≤ 6. It rejects a non-elementwise op in the epilogue that reads a hero.
- The multi-output fusion pass merges concatenate fusions only if the result keeps the concatenate emitter.

🎯 Justification
Equal-shaped concatenates over the same inputs, as in the Eigh expander's Jacobi permutations, ran as separate kernels or fell back to the loop emitter. Now they run as one kernel that reads each operand once. This also merges RoPE q/k concatenate pairs in some models.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:  ⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
This Eigh example gets a ~20% improvement on MI350:

```bash
HloModule Test
ENTRY Random_1000 {
  a.1 = f32[1000,1000]{1,0} parameter(0)
  ROOT CC = (f32[1000,1000]{1,0}, f32[1000]{0}) custom-call(a.1), custom_call_target="Eigh", backend_config="1,1,15,0.000010"
}
```

On gpt_j_6b, the RoPE q/k pairs merge in every transformer layer, but the overall end-to-end performance change is negligible.

🧪 Unit Tests:
hlo_fusion_analysis_test.cc and multi_output_fusion_test.cc cover the accepted shapes, the operand budget, mismatched splits and shapes, hero reads through non-elementwise ops (including inside the second sibling), and a layer-norm producer reduced from AlphaFold 3. Two FileCheck tests in emitters/tests/concatenate/ cover shape-changing epilogues and a shared hero.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both FileCheck tests also run gpu_test_correctness on one GPU.

head_commit.message:
Support BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm in CUDA BlasLt

Heuristic indices returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic` depend on the GPU and cuBLASLt version, so the same index can resolve to a different kernel across devices or library updates.

Therefore this change introduces `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` (and its proto representation `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` in `xla/stream_executor/gpu/gpu_blas_lt.proto`) to capture the full cuBLASLt algorithm configuration and numerical implementation flags. `cuda::BlasLt::MatmulPlan` implements `GetBlasLtMatmulAlgorithm` and `GetMatmulAlgorithm` to extract and reconstruct `cublasLtMatmulAlgo_t` descriptors, and `MatmulPlan::SetCachedAlgorithm` and `BlasLt::GetOrCreateMatmulPlanWithAlgorithm` add overloads accepting `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep row-local scan dimensions untiled in TilingSpace::GetValidTilings.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep row-local scan dimensions untiled in TilingSpace::GetValidTilings.

`PriorityFusion` fuses arbitrary producers into Triton scan fusions when the scan dimension has at most 128 elements (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`), relying on the invariant that row-local scans are covered by a single tile without a sequential loop. However, `TilingSpace::GetValidTilings` enumerated smaller power-of-two sequential tile sizes for `kScan` dimensions, allowing `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` on B200 to pick `sequential_tile_sizes=[2]` (a 2-iteration sequential loop) for a scan of dimension 3.

Keep sequential `kScan` dimensions with `dimension_size <= 128` untiled in `TilingSpace::GetValidTilings` so that row-local scans always receive a single tile of `PowerOf2Ceil(dimension_size)`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, so passing the same instruction twice checks every parameter.
2. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005776439

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

`EstimateNumWarps` previously computed `largest_live_tile_size` using raw padded element counts across all instructions in the tiled computation. For fusions with broadcasted inputs, `iota`, or sub-32-bit intermediate tiles (such as `pred` comparisons feeding a reduction), this inflated `largest_live_tile_size` by 4x or more and selected 4-8 warps where 2-4 warps are faster.

Introduce `GetLiveTileSizeForNumWarps`:

- Keep full padded element counts for operands and roots so global memory vectorization is unchanged.
- Ignore non-root `broadcast` and `constant` tiles, which do not materialize a separate register array beyond their operands, and size non-root `iota` by its 1D range along `iota_dimension`.
- Scale other intermediate array tiles by `min(element_bytes, 4) / 4` (32-bit register words).

Also account for multi-block SM residency (`blocks_per_core`) when computing `active_threads_per_core` in `EstimateRunTimeForTiledHloComputationImpl` so that 1-warp and 2-warp candidates on multi-wave grids are not penalized as if only a single block could reside on each SM.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1006120810

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Check unnormalized dot shapes in `upcaster_filter`

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Check unnormalized dot shapes in `upcaster_filter`

After `DotDimensionSorter` and `DotDecomposer` were removed from the early part of `GpuCompiler::OptimizeHloModule` in favor of running `DotDimensionNormalizer` later in the pipeline, `ResultCaster` and `OperandUpcaster` now inspect `dot` instructions before their contracting/non-contracting dimensions are flattened and before `GpuLayoutAssignment` assigns physical layouts.

Because `IsCublasSupportedMatMul` assumed normalized dot dimensions (`Rank(kContracting) == 1`, `Rank(kNonContracting) <= 1`, and non-minor batch dimensions), `upcaster_filter` falsely treated multi-dimensional mixed-precision dots (such as `f16 x f16 -> f32` attention einsums with multiple contracting or non-contracting dimensions) as unsupported by cuBLAS and upcasted their `f16` operands to `f32`.

Add `bool is_normalized = true` to `IsCublasSupportedMatMul` and pass `/*is_normalized=*/false` from `upcaster_filter` so that dots that will be normalized into valid 2D/batched GEMMs by `DotDimensionNormalizer` and `GpuLayoutAssignment` retain their mixed-precision operands.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007709070

display_title: `ConstraintPropagator` seeded 16-bit floating-point intervals on every instruction across all computations—clamping intermediate 32-bit reduction accumulators inside fused computations to `[-65504, 65504]`—did not propagate `get-tuple-element` user bounds across tuple-returning fusion boundaries, and only split output bounds across `add` operands when one operand was constant. Consequently, fusions combining a non-constant `add` with a large-reduction `convolution` inside a tuple-returning `kOutput` fusion received unconstrained inputs and overflowed to `inf` or `nan` in bfloat16.

head_commit.message:
`ConstraintPropagator` seeded 16-bit floating-point intervals on every instruction across all computations—clamping intermediate 32-bit reduction accumulators inside fused computations to `[-65504, 65504]`—did not propagate `get-tuple-element` user bounds across tuple-returning fusion boundaries, and only split output bounds across `add` operands when one operand was constant. Consequently, fusions combining a non-constant `add` with a large-reduction `convolution` inside a tuple-returning `kOutput` fusion received unconstrained inputs and overflowed to `inf` or `nan` in bfloat16.

Restrict `Seed16BitFloatingInstruction` in `ConstraintPropagator` to entry computation roots (recursing into `kTuple`, `kFusion`, and `kCall` roots), propagate `kGetTupleElement` user intervals to matching elements of tuple-returning callee roots in `PropagateComputationBoundary`, and split symmetric magnitude bounds across non-constant `kAdd` operands in `PropagateAddApprox`

display_title: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR3)

head_commit.message:
[ROCm profiler] Read advanced_configuration in the ROCm GpuTracer

Third of three changes to support ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration
in the ROCm tracer. Connects the parser to GpuTracer and deprecates
--xla_gpu_rocm_max_trace_events, which keeps working as the default
until remote capture forwards the gpu_* keys.

On Start(), GpuTracer sets its defaults (4M annotation strings, 4M
callback and activity events, all GPUs) and applies the gpu_* keys.
gpu_max_activity_api_events is accepted but not enforced yet.

A bad key does not fail Start(): valid keys are still applied, and the
diagnostics go to XSpace.errors/warnings in CollectData(), or to the
log if the tracer fails to start. With raise_error_on_start_failure,
any error fails Start() with InvalidArgument.

The flag logs a warning when set, and its help text and proto comment
say it is deprecated. The field is not marked [deprecated = true],
since the flag still sets it. The flag still replaces the 4M default for
both event caps, and each gpu_max_* key overrides only its own cap.
Remote capture forwards only a fixed set of advanced_configuration keys,
so its callers still need the flag; the warning, the help text and the
drop report say so. A later change removes the flag and reserves field
449.

The collector counts the events it drops at the callback event limit,
including ROCTX markers, and Export() reports them once per session in
the log and XSpace.warnings, as CUPTI does, instead of logging every
dropped HIP call. The report names the gpu_max_* key to raise and, for
remote capture, the flag.

Tests: rocm_collector_test adds CallbackCapDropsEventsBeyondLimit and
CallbackCapDropsAreReportedInEverySession, and checks the report for
ROCTX markers. New GPU test device_tracer_rocm_test covers a bad key,
a warning in XSpace, raise_error_on_start_failure, the callback limit
key and its drop report, the deprecated flag, and the key overriding
the flag.

display_title: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR2)

head_commit.message:
[ROCm profiler] Add rocm_tracer_options_utils

Second of three changes to support ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration
in the ROCm tracer. Adds the parser; nothing calls it yet.

UpdateRocmTracerOptionsFromProfilerOptions applies the gpu_* keys over
the caller's defaults and returns every problem as an error or warning,
instead of stopping at the first one as CUPTI does.
AppendOptionDiagnostics writes them to XSpace.errors/warnings and the
log.

- Event and annotation limits: a negative value is an error, and a
  value above kMaxRocmTraceEvents (1e9, now a shared constant with a
  static_assert that it fits the collector's int counters) is clamped.
  For the two event limits, 0 means no limit, as on CUDA, and becomes
  kMaxRocmTraceEvents with a warning; passed through, it would empty
  the trace. gpu_max_annotation_strings = 0 retains none, as on CUDA,
  and draws a warning. gpu_max_activity_api_events is stored but not
  enforced yet, because the collector only counts HIP_API activity
  events; a warning says so.
- gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task: 0 or more than the device count
  means every GPU, as on CUDA. A negative value is an error. A smaller
  value draws a warning that every GPU is still traced.
- Keys CUPTI implements but ROCm does not draw a "no effect" warning,
  unless the value asks for what ROCm already does.
  gpu_pm_sample_interval_us and gpu_pm_sample_buffer_size_per_gpu_mb
  only warn when gpu_pm_sample_counters names a counter, since CUDA
  ignores them otherwise.
- Unknown gpu_* keys are errors. Other keys belong to other profiler
  components and are ignored.

cupti_tracer_options_utils.cc gets a comment to keep the two key lists
in sync, and EveryCuptiKeyIsRecognized enforces it: it reads the CUPTI
parser's source and fails if ROCm neither applies nor warns about one of
its keys. The RocmTraceCollectorOptions comments drop "if -1, no limit",
which never applied to these unsigned fields.

Tests: rocm_tracer_options_utils_test, 30 host-only cases.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: #HloDiff Match aligned entry parameters by parameter number.

head_commit.message:
#HloDiff Match aligned entry parameters by parameter number.

Entry parameter numbers define the module signature, but parameter numbers are
excluded from fingerprints, so entry parameters could be cross-matched by shape
or graph structure, e.g. (x, y) -> x - y vs. (y, x) -> x - y, or when one
parameter changes its shape. If both entry computations have the same number of
parameters and at least half of them have compatible shapes at the same
position, match all entry parameters by number first.

With moved instructions (parent CL), (x, y) -> x - y vs. (y, x) -> x - y now
reports both parameters as moved, since each one is used at the other operand
position of the subtract. Parameters of called computations are not matched by
number, since their correspondence is defined by the call site operands.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007630935

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

When tiling `concatenate` regions in XTile, `SymbolicTileAnalysis` records branch-specific range constraints on each operand `Tile` (such as `offset in [0, N)` inside its active `scf.if` branch), but `EvaluateTilingParameters` previously ignored `TiledHloInstruction::tile().constraints()` when constructing the `IndexingMap` for `xla.apply_indexing`. As a result, `IsGuaranteedInBounds` evaluated the unconstrained `IndexingMap` domain across all `concatenate` branches—which can include negative offsets or offsets exceeding an individual operand's dimension—forcing unnecessary per-element bounds masks (`arith.cmpi` + `arith.andi`) on tile-aligned `concatenate` operand loads.

Add `tile_constraints` to `offset_indexing_map` and call `offset_indexing_map.Simplify()` before `emitters::ApplyIndexing` in `EvaluateTilingParameters` so `xla.apply_indexing` carries the constrained and simplified `IndexingMap` directly, and use `xla::GetRange` in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004246686

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Optimize `xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty` by caching emptiness in `bool empty_`.

head_commit.message:
Optimize `xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty` by caching emptiness in `bool empty_`.

`xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty()` (called by `HloInstruction::has_backend_config()`) previously acquired `absl::MutexLock lock(mutex_)` on every call just to check `proto_ == nullptr && raw_string_.empty()`. When multiple threads concurrently query `has_backend_config()` on shared HLO instructions, they heavily contend on `BackendConfigWrapper::mutex_`.

This change:
- Tracks whether `BackendConfigWrapper` is empty in a `bool empty_ = true;` member updated on construction and move-assignment, allowing `empty()` to read `empty_` without locking `mutex_`.
- Adds fast paths to `BackendConfigWrapper::operator==` (`this == &other` and `empty() && other.empty()`) to avoid mutex acquisition and string formatting when comparing empty configs.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007589856

name: CI ROCm
display_title: #HloDiff Report matched instructions with differently wired uses as moved.

head_commit.message:
#HloDiff Report matched instructions with differently wired uses as moved.

A matched instruction pair whose instructions are identical (same canonical
fingerprint) can still be wired differently, e.g. sin and cos in
`sin(x) - cos(x)` vs. `cos(x) - sin(x)`. Such pairs were reported as unchanged,
so the diff showed no difference at all. They are now reported as moved.

How a pair is classified (changed takes precedence, so the four kinds stay
disjoint):

1.  Fingerprints differ: changed.
2.  Otherwise, if its uses differ in a way that is not explained (below): moved.
3.  Otherwise: unchanged.

Uses are compared as operand slots, i.e. (user, operand index) pairs. Left users
are translated to the right through the mapping, and unmatched users are
skipped, since they are already reported as unmatched. Commutative binary users
(add, multiply, ...) ignore the operand index. If the slot multisets differ, the
instruction occupying each differing slot on the other side is looked at, and
the difference is explained if that instruction is:

*   unmatched, e.g. `sub(sin, cos)` vs. `sub(sin, tanh)` doesn't make cos
    moved, since tanh is reported as unmatched;
*   computing the same value (equal hash of its subgraph), e.g. two identical
    `sin(x)` that the matcher cross-matched; or
*   a look-alike (same fingerprint) where one of the mappings was made by a
    similarity-based matcher, which likely picked the wrong one of several
    candidates. This doesn't apply if the difference is a permutation of the
    same user's operands, which is a real swap.

| left            | right           | result                                |
| --------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `sub(sin, cos)` | `sub(cos, sin)` | sin, cos: moved                       |
| `add(sin, cos)` | `add(cos, sin)` | nothing (commutative)                 |
| `sub(s0, s1)`, `s0`, `s1` identical, cross-matched | same | nothing |
| `neg(sin)`      | `neg(sin)`, `abs(sin)` | nothing (`abs` is unmatched)   |

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007587659

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Add BackendConfigWrapper::content_id()

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Add BackendConfigWrapper::content_id()

Backends derive values from backend configs on hot paths, and custom calls that
embed a kernel carry configs of several megabytes. A cache of derived values
must notice when a config changes. The address of the wrapper cannot tell,
because ApplyFnOnProto mutates the wrapper in place.
BackendConfigWrapper::content_id() returns an id of the current contents that
changes whenever they change, and ids are never reused.
HloInstruction::backend_config_content_id() exposes it, so backends can key
caches of derived values by it.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005841220

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated), and checks internal uses of an in-place fusion parameter before sharing buffers.
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, per-path `DynamicSlice` tracking, `"dynamic_slice_fusion"` custom fusions, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005776439

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [Pathways] Canonicalize HLO program names in keys

head_commit.message:
[Pathways] Canonicalize HLO program names in keys

MPMD program stages often compile to identical executables, but their cache
keys differ in the module name and the Shardy mesh names. The new flag
`--pathways_compilation_cache_canonicalize_hlo_program_names`, true by default,
makes keys canonicalize mesh names, and the module name unless TPU flags depend
on it.
Existing single flight deduplication then compiles each distinct stage once.
Stages that share a compilation keep their own IFRT executable names, but their
TPU metadata comes from the compiled program. The flag must match on clients
and servers, and persistent cache keys of named programs change once.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Convert <=8-bit integer and F32 dot operands to BF16 by default

Every <=8-bit integer value (`S1`, `U1`, `S2`, `U2`, `S4`, `U4`, `S8`, `U8`) is
losslessly representable in `BF16` (which has 8 significand bits). Previously,
`DotOperandConverter` upcasted the integer operand of a mixed `(int<=8, f32)`
`dot` to `F32`, forcing the `dot` onto the TF32 Tensor Core path
(`dot(f32, f32) -> f32`) even when `PrecisionConfig` had default precision
(`ALG_UNSET` and `DEFAULT` operand precision).

Update `DotOperandConverter` so that when a `dot` with `F32` or `BF16` output
and default precision multiplies an <=8-bit integer operand by an `F32` operand
on a target that supports fast `BF16` GEMMs (Ampere+ on CUDA, or ROCm GPUs with
`BF16` support excluding MI200) and `tensor_float_32_execution_enabled()` is
true, both operands are converted to `BF16` (`dot(bf16, bf16) -> f32`/`bf16`).
Explicit higher precision requests (`HIGH`, `HIGHEST`, explicit `DotAlgorithm`s,
or disabled TF32 execution) and targets without `BF16` GEMM support continue to
upcast to `F32`.

display_title: Deduplicate op-independent conversion helpers in `hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo`.

head_commit.message:
Deduplicate op-independent conversion helpers in `hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo`.

`HloToStablehloOpConverter<StablehloOpTy>` and `HloToStablehloCustomCallOpConverter<HloOpTy>` instantiate conversion patterns across all ~135 StableHLO and MHLO operations in `xla/mlir_hlo/mhlo/transforms/hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo/hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo.cc`. Previously, `convertAttributes`, `isDenseI64Array`, `convertDenseArray`, and `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` were templated on `HloOpTy` / `StablehloOpTy` without `if constexpr`, causing `convertAttributes` and the region-inlining loop to be emitted separately for every op (and requiring an explicit 11-op `if constexpr` exclusion list in `convertAttributes` for MHLO-only ops without a `HloToStablehloOp` mapping). In addition, `hasPrivateFeaturesNotInStablehlo<HloOpTy>` checked the 10 XLA-private op types via runtime `isa<...>` in every pattern instantiation rather than compile-time `if constexpr`.

Make `isDenseI64Array`, `convertDenseArray`, `convertAttributes`, `convertTypesAndAttributes`, `convertRegions`, and `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` non-template helpers operating on `Operation*`, check `hasPrivateFeaturesNotInStablehlo<HloOpTy>` at compile time with `if constexpr (llvm::is_one_of<HloOpTy, ...>::value)`, and guard `convertRegions` with `if constexpr (!HloOpTy::template hasTrait<OpTrait::ZeroRegions>())`. In addition, hoist `dyn_cast<mhlo::CustomCallOp>(hloOp)` out of the attribute loop in `convertAttributes`, mutate `NamedAttribute` values in place (`hloAttr.setValue(stablehloAttr)`), fetch `hloAttr.getName().getValue()` only after `dyn_cast<DenseIntElementsAttr>` succeeds in `convertDenseArray`, and pass `getPublicFeaturesNotInStablehlo(hloOp)` into `rewriteMhloOpAsCustomCall` instead of recomputing it.

Runtime and memory performance impact: Zero memory overhead (`+0.00%` allocations and peak memory) and `-2.23%` faster geomean CPU time (`-2.24%` wall time) across 8 `createHloLegalizeToStablehloPass` microbenchmarks.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [Pathways] Canonicalize HLO program names in keys

head_commit.message:
[Pathways] Canonicalize HLO program names in keys

MPMD program stages often compile to identical executables, but their cache
keys differ in the module name and the Shardy mesh names. The new flag
`--pathways_compilation_cache_canonicalize_hlo_program_names`, true by default,
makes keys canonicalize mesh names, and the module name unless TPU flags depend
on it.
Existing single flight deduplication then compiles each distinct stage once.
Stages that share a compilation keep their own IFRT executable names, but their
TPU metadata comes from the compiled program. The flag must match on clients
and servers, and persistent cache keys of named programs change once.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

head_commit.message:
Break ties between ready async-done instructions by data dependency.

When two supported async-done candidates are otherwise tied in
`ReadySetLt::AIsBetterThanB`, the scheduler falls back to the original
instruction order. For example, when two dependent layers each offload their
result to host, the input order may list the deeper layer's copy-done first,
which delays the earlier layer's offload past the next layer's compute and
completes the offloads in reverse dependency order.

Add a `kAsyncDoneDataDependency` tie-breaker before `kOriginalOrder`: if an
input of one async-start reaches the other async-start (via the schedule
graph's reachability map), the done transferring the earlier-produced data
completes first in program order. Unrelated async-dones are unaffected and keep
their original order.

head_commit.message:
Optimize `xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty` by caching emptiness in `bool empty_`.

`xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty()` (called by `HloInstruction::has_backend_config()`) previously acquired `absl::MutexLock lock(mutex_)` on every call just to check `proto_ == nullptr && raw_string_.empty()`. - Tracks whether `BackendConfigWrapper` is empty in a `bool empty_ = true;` member updated on construction and move-assignment, allowing `empty()` to read `empty_` without locking `mutex_`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: #HloDiff Report matched instructions with differently wired uses as moved.

head_commit.message:
#HloDiff Report matched instructions with differently wired uses as moved.

A matched instruction pair whose instructions are identical (same canonical
fingerprint) can still be wired differently, e.g. sin and cos in
`sin(x) - cos(x)` vs. `cos(x) - sin(x)`. Such pairs were reported as unchanged,
so the diff showed no difference at all. They are now reported as moved.

How a pair is classified (changed takes precedence, so the four kinds stay
disjoint):

1.  Fingerprints differ: changed.
2.  Otherwise, if its uses differ in a way that is not explained (below): moved.
3.  Otherwise: unchanged.

Uses are compared as operand slots, i.e. (user, operand index) pairs. Left users
are translated to the right through the mapping, and unmatched users are
skipped, since they are already reported as unmatched. Commutative binary users
(add, multiply, ...) ignore the operand index. If the slot multisets differ, the
instruction occupying each differing slot on the other side is looked at, and
the difference is explained if that instruction is:

*   unmatched, e.g. `sub(sin, cos)` vs. `sub(sin, tanh)` doesn't make cos
    moved, since tanh is reported as unmatched;
*   computing the same value (equal hash of its subgraph), e.g. two identical
    `sin(x)` that the matcher cross-matched; or
*   a look-alike (same fingerprint) where one of the mappings was made by a
    similarity-based matcher, which likely picked the wrong one of several
    candidates. This doesn't apply if the difference is a permutation of the
    same user's operands, which is a real swap.

| left            | right           | result                                |
| --------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `sub(sin, cos)` | `sub(cos, sin)` | sin, cos: moved                       |
| `add(sin, cos)` | `add(cos, sin)` | nothing (commutative)                 |
| `sub(s0, s1)`, `s0`, `s1` identical, cross-matched | same | nothing |
| `neg(sin)`      | `neg(sin)`, `abs(sin)` | nothing (`abs` is unmatched)   |

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated), and checks internal uses of an in-place fusion parameter before sharing buffers.
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, per-path `DynamicSlice` tracking, `"dynamic_slice_fusion"` custom fusions, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

display_title: Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

In `GpuAliasInfo`, a fused keys-only `sort` has an array output shape (`user_index == {}`), so comparing `user_index` against `ShapeIndex{0}` always rejected in-place buffer sharing. Only compare against the operand index when the `sort` output is a tuple, and require `user_index.empty()` otherwise.

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate tile constraints in XTile indexing emission to elide bounds masks.

When tiling `concatenate` regions in XTile, `SymbolicTileAnalysis` records branch-specific range constraints on each operand `Tile` (such as `offset in [0, N)` inside its active `scf.if` branch), but `EvaluateTilingParameters` previously ignored `TiledHloInstruction::tile().constraints()` when constructing the `IndexingMap` for `xla.apply_indexing`. As a result, `IsGuaranteedInBounds` evaluated the unconstrained `IndexingMap` domain across all `concatenate` branches—which can include negative offsets or offsets exceeding an individual operand's dimension—forcing unnecessary per-element bounds masks (`arith.cmpi` + `arith.andi`) on tile-aligned `concatenate` operand loads.

Add `tile_constraints` to `offset_indexing_map` and call `offset_indexing_map.Simplify()` before `emitters::ApplyIndexing` in `EvaluateTilingParameters` so `xla.apply_indexing` carries the constrained and simplified `IndexingMap` directly, and use `xla::GetRange` in `IsGuaranteedInBounds` and `TritonXlaCollapseContiguousMinorDimsPass`.

display_title: Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

In `GpuAliasInfo`, a fused keys-only `sort` has an array output shape (`user_index == {}`), so comparing `user_index` against `ShapeIndex{0}` always rejected in-place buffer sharing. Only compare against the operand index when the `sort` output is a tuple, and require `user_index.empty()` otherwise.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated), and checks internal uses of an in-place fusion parameter before sharing buffers.
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, per-path `DynamicSlice` tracking, `"dynamic_slice_fusion"` custom fusions, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

head_commit.message:
Optimize `xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty` by caching emptiness in `bool empty_`.

`xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty()` (called by `HloInstruction::has_backend_config()`) previously acquired `absl::MutexLock lock(mutex_)` on every call just to check `proto_ == nullptr && raw_string_.empty()`. When multiple threads concurrently query `has_backend_config()` on shared HLO instructions, they heavily contend on `BackendConfigWrapper::mutex_`.

This change:
- Tracks whether `BackendConfigWrapper` is empty in a `bool empty_ = true;` member updated on construction and move-assignment, allowing `empty()` to read `empty_` without locking `mutex_`.
- Adds fast paths to `BackendConfigWrapper::operator==` (`this == &other` and `empty() && other.empty()`) to avoid mutex acquisition and string formatting when comparing empty configs.

display_title: PR #50225: [XLA:GPU] Support multi-output fusion in the concatenate emitter

head_commit.message:
PR #50225: [XLA:GPU] Support multi-output fusion in the concatenate emitter

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50225

📝 Summary of Changes
- The concatenate emitter emits fusions with several roots. Each distinct hero is computed once per operand loop, and one shared epilogue writes all outputs.
- UseConcatenateFusion accepts several roots when the heroes are concatenates with identical splits, the roots share one shape, and roots × operands ≤ 6. It rejects a non-elementwise op in the epilogue that reads a hero.
- The multi-output fusion pass merges concatenate fusions only if the result keeps the concatenate emitter.

🎯 Justification
Equal-shaped concatenates over the same inputs, as in the Eigh expander's Jacobi permutations, ran as separate kernels or fell back to the loop emitter. Now they run as one kernel that reads each operand once. This also merges RoPE q/k concatenate pairs in some models.

🚀 Kind of Contribution:  ⚡️ Performance Improvement,

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
This Eigh example gets a ~20% improvement on MI350:

```bash
HloModule Test
ENTRY Random_1000 {
  a.1 = f32[1000,1000]{1,0} parameter(0)
  ROOT CC = (f32[1000,1000]{1,0}, f32[1000]{0}) custom-call(a.1), custom_call_target="Eigh", backend_config="1,1,15,0.000010"
}
```

On gpt_j_6b, the RoPE q/k pairs merge in every transformer layer, but the overall end-to-end performance change is negligible.

🧪 Unit Tests:
hlo_fusion_analysis_test.cc and multi_output_fusion_test.cc cover the accepted shapes, the operand budget, mismatched splits and shapes, hero reads through non-elementwise ops (including inside the second sibling), and a layer-norm producer reduced from AlphaFold 3. Two FileCheck tests in emitters/tests/concatenate/ cover shape-changing epilogues and a shared hero.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Both FileCheck tests also run gpu_test_correctness on one GPU.

head_commit.message:
Optimize `xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty` by caching emptiness in `bool empty_`.

`xla::BackendConfigWrapper::empty()` (called by `HloInstruction::has_backend_config()`) previously acquired `absl::MutexLock lock(mutex_)` on every call just to check `proto_ == nullptr && raw_string_.empty()`. When multiple threads concurrently query `has_backend_config()` on shared HLO instructions, they heavily contend on `BackendConfigWrapper::mutex_`.

This change:
- Tracks whether `BackendConfigWrapper` is empty in a `bool empty_ = true;` member updated on construction and move-assignment, allowing `empty()` to read `empty_` without locking `mutex_`.
- Adds fast paths to `BackendConfigWrapper::operator==` (`this == &other` and `empty() && other.empty()`) to avoid mutex acquisition and string formatting when comparing empty configs.

display_title: Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

head_commit.message:
Check all operand uses before sharing buffers

When an instruction reads a value through several positions (e.g. `x` and `bitcast(x)`) or through several operands (e.g. `fusion(x, x)`), all of them are backed by the same buffer. But `BufferAssigner::LiveRangeInterferes` allowed the user to reuse that buffer if any consumed position allowed it, and `HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only checked the defining position. So an in-place fusion could overwrite elements of its input before reading them through the bitcast.

Therefore this change adds `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser`, which requires every use of the operand value by the user to allow sharing, and uses it in both places. This is the same per-use check that copy insertion already does. Also:

1. `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` checks all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand, rejects the `GetInPlaceInputOutputPairs` fast-path when the same operand is also passed in another operand position (unless disjoint read/write regions are annotated), and checks internal uses of an in-place fusion parameter before sharing buffers.
2. `DoesNotUseOperandBuffer` checks all uses of the operand value at a loop fusion instead of returning early on the first dead fusion parameter.
3. `GpuAliasInfo` checks the paths from all fusion parameters that correspond to the operand (including internal ops consuming a parameter twice, per-path `DynamicSlice` tracking, `"dynamic_slice_fusion"` custom fusions, variadic scatter output indices, and non-elementwise multi-output fusion roots), since its hint takes precedence over the generic fusion logic.
4. `NVPTXAliasInfo` rejects in-place `all-reduce` and `collective-broadcast` when the same operand appears more than once.

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51490

head_commit.message:
`IndexingMap::MergeModConstraints` tightens the bounds of `x` for a point constraint `x mod div == res` using `(bound / div) * div + res`. Because C++ division rounds toward zero while `llvm::mod` uses a nonnegative Euclidean remainder, negative bounds with a positive remainder are shifted by `div`.

Move each bound inward by the Euclidean distance in `[0, div - 1]` using `llvm::mod`, and reset the map to known empty when `lo > hi`.

threading", https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/235294) makes

IFRT and Pathways call sites to ensure thread safety during concurrent

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse producers into Triton scan fusions with a scan dimension above 128 (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`) when the producer has only effective-scalar operands and consists of only effective-scalar parameters, effective-scalar constants, `iota`, broadcasts of effective scalars, and elementwise operations (`IsCheapNoMemoryProducer`).

Fusing these memoryless producers avoids materializing full-size intermediate broadcast or mask tensors in global memory when a scan has an epilogue that broadcasts scalar thresholds or compares against `iota`. On `f32[256, N]` cumsum with an elementwise epilogue (`N` in `{131072, 262144}`) and `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` enabled, this reduces execution from 3 kernels before this change to 1 kernel, speeding up H100 by 1.7x (230–457 µs to 134–266 µs) and B200 by 2.0x (161–322 µs to 80–156 µs, 2.3x faster than the default emitter).

With default flags, this change has no effect.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Avoid rewriting degenerate, non-minor, or loop-splitting small scans in ScanRewriterTriton.

Restrict `ScanRewriterTriton::IsEligibleScan` to skip scans where `AssociativeScanRewriter` combined with native `kLoop` or `kInput` fusions produces fewer kernel launches or better memory coalescing:

1. Require `scan_dim_size > 1` so degenerate single-element scans are left to `AssociativeScanRewriter` instead of launching a Triton kernel.
2. Require the scan dimension to be the most minor physical dimension of the input layout (`LayoutUtil::Minor(input_shape.layout(), 0) == scan_dim`) when a layout is present, ensuring coalesced memory accesses along the scan dimension.
3. Reject small scans (`scan_dim_size <= 1024`) without a `kCustom` fusion producer when their bounded non-effective-scalar producer or consumer neighborhood (walking through elementwise ops, `kBroadcast`, `kBitcast`, and `kReshape`) touches a loop or input data-movement or indexing op (`kConcatenate`, `kDynamicSlice`, `kDynamicUpdateSlice`, `kGather`, `kPad`, `kReverse`, `kScatter`, `kSlice`). For scans up to 3 radix-16 reduction levels, keeping the lowered scan in the surrounding native fusion avoids splitting the fusion around a standalone Triton scan kernel.

With default flags, this change has no effect.

display_title: Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

In `GpuAliasInfo`, a fused keys-only `sort` has an array output shape (`user_index == {}`), so comparing `user_index` against `ShapeIndex{0}` always rejected in-place buffer sharing. display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

head_commit.message:
`IndexingMap::MergeModConstraints` tightens the bounds of `x` for a point constraint `x mod div == res` using `(bound / div) * div + res`. Because C++ division rounds toward zero while `llvm::mod` uses a nonnegative Euclidean remainder, negative bounds with a positive remainder are shifted by `div`.

Move each bound inward by the Euclidean distance in `[0, div - 1]` using `llvm::mod`, and reset the map to known empty when `lo > hi`.

Decouple CUB radix sort scratch estimation from runtime FFI handlers.

`xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_keys` and `xla.gpu.ext.cub_sort_pairs` bundled compile-time scratch-size estimation (`CubSort{Keys,Pairs}Instantiate`) on the runtime execution FFI targets. display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

display_title: Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

In `GpuAliasInfo`, a fused keys-only `sort` has an array output shape (`user_index == {}`), so comparing `user_index` against `ShapeIndex{0}` always rejected in-place buffer sharing. Only compare against the operand index when the `sort` output is a tuple, and require `user_index.empty()` otherwise.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

- Profiled costs are keyed by the instruction's OpMetadata.scheduling_name,
  the name the scheduler knew it by, rather than by its final name. Passes
  after scheduling rename instructions (e.g. ConvertAsyncCollectivesToSync),
  so e.g. a synchronous all-reduce in the profile was not found when
  compiling again.
- AllocateBuffer custom calls only reserve a buffer and launch nothing, so
  they never appear in a profile. The GPU scheduler treats them as no-ops:
  they are not reported as missing, and their fallback cost is 0 rather than
  the 1000 us of a generic custom call (524 such instructions per DeepSeek-v3
  training step, i.e. 0.5 s of fictitious compute the scheduler believed it
  could hide collectives behind).
- No cost is expected for the condition of a while loop with a known trip
  count, which the GPU runtime never evaluates, so the GPU profile statistics
  aggregator no longer reports its instructions as missing.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep row-local scan dimensions untiled in TilingSpace::GetValidTilings.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep row-local scan dimensions untiled in TilingSpace::GetValidTilings.

`PriorityFusion` fuses arbitrary producers into Triton scan fusions when the scan dimension has at most 128 elements (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`), relying on the invariant that row-local scans are covered by a single tile without a sequential loop. However, `TilingSpace::GetValidTilings` enumerated smaller power-of-two sequential tile sizes for `kScan` dimensions, allowing `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` on B200 to pick `sequential_tile_sizes=[2]` (a 2-iteration sequential loop) for a scan of dimension 3.

Expose `kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize = 128` in `tiling_space.h` (and use it in `priority_fusion.cc`), and keep sequential `kScan` dimensions with `dimension_size <= kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize` untiled in `TilingSpace::GetValidTilings` so that row-local scans always receive a single tile of `PowerOf2Ceil(dimension_size)`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse producers into Triton scan fusions with a scan dimension above 128 (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`) when the producer has only effective-scalar operands and consists of only effective-scalar parameters, effective-scalar constants, `iota`, broadcasts of effective scalars, and elementwise operations (`IsCheapNoMemoryProducer`).

Fusing these memoryless producers avoids materializing full-size intermediate broadcast or mask tensors in global memory when a scan has an epilogue that broadcasts scalar thresholds or compares against `iota`. On `f32[256, N]` cumsum with an elementwise epilogue (`N` in `{131072, 262144}`) and `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` enabled, this reduces execution from 3 kernels before this change to 1 kernel, speeding up H100 by 1.7x (230–457 µs to 134–266 µs) and B200 by 2.0x (161–322 µs to 80–156 µs, 2.3x faster than the default emitter).

With default flags, this change has no effect.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Keep row-local scan dimensions untiled in TilingSpace::GetValidTilings.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Keep row-local scan dimensions untiled in TilingSpace::GetValidTilings.

`PriorityFusion` fuses arbitrary producers into Triton scan fusions when the scan dimension has at most 128 elements (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`), relying on the invariant that row-local scans are covered by a single tile without a sequential loop. However, `TilingSpace::GetValidTilings` enumerated smaller power-of-two sequential tile sizes for `kScan` dimensions, allowing `GpuIndexingPerformanceModel` on B200 to pick `sequential_tile_sizes=[2]` (a 2-iteration sequential loop) for a scan of dimension 3.

Expose `kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize = 128` in `tiling_space.h` (and use it in `priority_fusion.cc`), and keep sequential `kScan` dimensions with `dimension_size <= kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize` untiled in `TilingSpace::GetValidTilings` so that row-local scans always receive a single tile of `PowerOf2Ceil(dimension_size)`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007059856

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Set unique collective op_id on CPU and compute per-call Gloo tags.

head_commit.message:
Set unique collective op_id on CPU and compute per-call Gloo tags.

Previously, `ThunkEmitter` set `op_id` on every collective thunk to `channel_id` when present or to the module ID otherwise, and `GlooCommunicator` hardcoded `tag = 0` on all collective operations. While the presence of `channel_id` (`has_channel_id`) still selects the collective group mode (such as `CROSS_PARTITION` or `FLATTENED_ID`), its numeric value was originally meant for matching collectives across separate modules in MPMD programs. In modern single-module SPMD programs, passes often set a constant dummy `channel_id` (such as `1`) just to mark `has_channel_id = true`, which gave multiple collectives in the same module the same `op_id`.

Update `GetCollectiveOpParams` in `xla/service/cpu/thunk_emitter.cc` to set `op_id` to `instruction->unique_id()`, giving each collective instruction in a module a distinct static ID while preserving `has_channel_id` for group-mode selection. In `xla/backends/cpu/collectives/gloo_communicator.cc`, track a per-`op_id` loop counter for the active `RunId` and fingerprint `(op_id, run_id, loop_counter)` into Gloo's 32-bit tag for `AllReduce`, `CollectivePermute`, `AllToAll`, `AllGather`, and `ReduceScatter`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fuse cheap scalar producers into large Triton scan fusions.

Allow `PriorityFusion` to fuse producers into Triton scan fusions with a scan dimension above 128 (`kMaxRowLocalScanDimSize`) when the producer has only effective-scalar operands and consists of only effective-scalar parameters, effective-scalar constants, `iota`, broadcasts of effective scalars, and elementwise operations (`IsCheapNoMemoryProducer`).

Fusing these memoryless producers avoids materializing full-size intermediate broadcast or mask tensors in global memory when a scan has an epilogue that broadcasts scalar thresholds or compares against `iota`. On `f32[256, N]` cumsum with an elementwise epilogue (`N` in `{131072, 262144}`) and `xla_gpu_experimental_enable_triton_scan` enabled, this reduces execution from 3 kernels before this change to 1 kernel, speeding up H100 by 1.7x (230–457 µs to 134–266 µs) and B200 by 2.0x (161–322 µs to 80–156 µs, 2.3x faster than the default emitter).

With default flags, this change has no effect.

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Fix three kinds of instruction that PGLE wrongly reported as missing from the profile

- Profiled costs are keyed by the instruction's OpMetadata.scheduling_name,
  the name the scheduler knew it by, rather than by its final name. Passes
  after scheduling rename instructions (e.g. ConvertAsyncCollectivesToSync),
  so e.g. a synchronous all-reduce in the profile was not found when
  compiling again.
- AllocateBuffer custom calls only reserve a buffer and launch nothing, so
  they never appear in a profile. The GPU scheduler treats them as no-ops:
  they are not reported as missing, and their fallback cost is 0 rather than
  the 1000 us of a generic custom call (524 such instructions per DeepSeek-v3
  training step, i.e. 0.5 s of fictitious compute the scheduler believed it
  could hide collectives behind).
- No cost is expected for the condition of a while loop with a known trip
  count, which the GPU runtime never evaluates, so the GPU profile statistics
  aggregator no longer reports its instructions as missing.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Check element types for kReduce and kReduceWindow in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Check element types for kReduce and kReduceWindow in FloatSupport::EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision.

Check that the output subshape and corresponding `to_apply` parameter types of `kReduce` and `kReduceWindow`, as well as any `kConvert` instructions in their `to_apply` subcomputation, have a precision-preserving element type transition relative to the reduced operand (`in_type == out_type` or between `high_precision_type_` and `low_precision_type_`).

Combined with the `kConvert` check in `EffectiveOperandPrecisionIsOutputPrecision`, this prevents `BFloat16Propagation` from propagating `BF16` through `kReduce` or `kReduceWindow` when the `to_apply` subcomputation narrows or truncates values (either via `kConvert`, such as `F32 -> S32 -> F32` or `F32 -> F16 -> F32`, or implicitly via mixed-precision parameter/output types), while still allowing same-type converts, conversions between `high_precision_type_` and `low_precision_type_`, and non-`kConvert` instructions of other element types (such as `PRED` predicates or `S32` variadic branches).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007330857

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Add parameter buffer slices to ComputationKernelArguments.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Add parameter buffer slices to ComputationKernelArguments.

`Visit` in `ComputationKernelArguments` previously added slices to `walk.arguments` only by iterating over `instruction->operands()` and skipped `kParameter` instructions when adding `instruction` slices to `walk.results`. When a called computation has an unused `kParameter` (or a `kParameter` that is the computation root with no other users), its slice was omitted from `buffer_table_index_`, causing `IrEmitter::EmitGlobalBufferPointer` to `CHECK`-fail when `IrEmitter::HandleParameter` visited the parameter.

Explicitly add `kParameter` slices to `walk.arguments` in `Visit` so every parameter visited by `IrEmitter` has a buffer table index. Every non-thread-local slice of a walked instruction is now in the buffer table, so `Fingerprint` checks this instead of handling buffers outside the table.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007325087

display_title: PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

head_commit.message:
PR #50583: [ROCm] [CUDA] Serve pinned_host buffers from host memory with the VMM allocator PR 3/3

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50583

Note on these PR chains:  diff here shows +877 lines because it has other two commits combined here , once those two PRs go in actual diff here is only +284. also all three PRs touch shared XLA GPU code.

## 📝 Summary of Changes

With the VMM allocator (`GpuAllocatorConfig::Kind::kVmm`), `pinned_host` buffers now come from pinned host memory instead of device memory, on CUDA and ROCm.

- The PJRT GPU client passes the VMM allocator the same per-device pinned host allocators the BFC path uses. It creates the allocator through the generic `DeviceAddressVmmAllocator::Create()`, so there are no CUDA/ROCm `#if` branches.
- Without a host allocator, `MemorySpace::kHost` requests now fail with `FailedPrecondition` instead of silently getting device memory.

Part 3 of 3; needs both:
1. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50581: VA remapping skips host memory space allocations
2. https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/50582: the VMM allocator serves `MemorySpace::kHost` from a host allocator
3. This PR. **Until PR 1 and PR 2 land, this branch also has their commits; only the last commit is new.**

## 🎯 Justification

For `kVmm`, nothing served the host memory space, so `pinned_host` buffers got device memory with no CPU mapping and any CPU access segfaulted. Orbax checkpointing does exactly that, so every JAX job with `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR=vmm` crashed at its first checkpoint save, on CUDA and ROCm. Command buffer update modes other than `ALWAYS_UPDATE` force the VMM allocator, so they crashed too.

VMM clients now behave like BFC clients for `pinned_host`: the same host memory limit (`XLA_PJRT_GPU_HOST_MEMORY_LIMIT_GB`) and preallocation setting apply, and host offloading actually moves data to host memory.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

## 🧪 Unit Tests

- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_test`: with VMM, a `pinned_host` buffer created from host data and a `pinned_host` program output are readable on the CPU.
- `se_gpu_pjrt_client_multi_gpu_test`: `pinned_host` buffers on two devices are readable on the CPU.
- `device_address_vmm_allocator_test`: `kHost` without a host allocator fails.

display_title: [XLA] Preserve result shape when simplifying scalar-predicate selects

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Preserve result shape when simplifying scalar-predicate selects

Select permits scalar predicates with tensor results. Folding boolean
selects directly to the predicate or its negation drops the result
shape and aborts in the instruction replacement check.

Broadcast scalar replacements to the original select shape, preserving
its layout. Add regression tests for both boolean branch orders.

display_title: Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

head_commit.message:
Fix variadic scatter and keys-only sort buffer sharing

For a bare variadic `scatter` whose inputs have the same shape, `HloDataflowAnalysis::CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` falls past the must-alias check when `user_index` points to another output tuple element, and then only checked `operand_indices[0] == 0`. That wrongly allowed input 0 to share its buffer with output `{1}`. Match `operand_indices[0]` against `user_index[0]` for tuple-shaped scatters instead.

In `GpuAliasInfo`, a fused keys-only `sort` has an array output shape (`user_index == {}`), so comparing `user_index` against `ShapeIndex{0}` always rejected in-place buffer sharing. Only compare against the operand index when the `sort` output is a tuple, and require `user_index.empty()` otherwise.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007219197

display_title: [XLA] Warm up the pinned host memory pool in `gpu_client_stream_error_test`

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Warm up the pinned host memory pool in `gpu_client_stream_error_test`

The test expects the resulting
`CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` to be reported from the stream.

However, it is actually racy: either the pinned host allocation for `ToLiteral()` or the actual `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` error from running the program may come first. The results in different error code.

On H100 the first CUDA call after the fault ends up being the pinned host allocation for the device-to-host staging buffer, which fails with the sticky error and gets reported as `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`.

Populate the pinned host pool with a trivial device-to-host transfer first, so the stream error is observed by the stream.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1007304365

display_title: Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

head_commit.message:
Let heap simulator reuse operands read through other positions

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Since `CanShareOperandValueBufferWithUser` checks every use of the value by the user, this restriction is no longer needed for correctness. So this change removes it, which lets the heap simulator reuse more operand buffers.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1005841220

display_title: Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

head_commit.message:
Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

When inherent_low_padding equals base_dilation_factor, SpaceToBatchConverter prepends one undilated element to each split and sets low_padding_for_conv to 0.

For each split of S undilated elements to produce S * base_dilation_factor outputs, the high-side overlap must be kernel_spatial_dim_size + base_dilation_factor - 2 rather than kernel_spatial_dim_size (which only matched for base_dilation_factor == 2). Therefore this change updates last_overlap in GetConvolutionDetails accordingly.

Also update the split-size loop in PropagateOnConv for base-dilated convolutions so it uses the actual low padding passed to HaloDuplicateWithSlice and does not count halo_size as available spatial size (since ChangeSpatialSizeOnSpaceToBatchedShape slices the collapsed spatial dimension to spatial_split_size * num_splits).

Fixes https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51365

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1004178625
